title: Cross-linking mass spectrometry guided structure prediction of disordered Encephalitozoon hellem proteins.
authors: Weyer, Elizabeth; Wang, Yongliang; Tomita, Tadakimi; Madrid-Aliste, Carlos; Nandigrami, Prithviraj; Fiser, Andras; Sidoli, Simone; Aguilan, Jennifer T; Han, Bing; Weiss, Louis M
one_liner_zh: 该文将交联质谱数据整合进AlphaFold类深度学习结构预测流程，用于预测无同源模板且含无序区的微孢子虫蛋白复合物结构，属于蛋白质结构预测与整合建模的方法创新，与课题高度相关。
abstract: Microsporidia such as Encephalitozoon hellem are obligate intracellular human parasites that remain genetically intractable, limiting the functional characterization of their proteomes. Experimental structural studies are challenging, as many proteins in microsporidia comprise a large percentage of disordered regions. Computational structural studies based on homology-based modeling and the use of deep-learning algorithms for microsporidian proteins also remain limited because most have little to no sequence similarity to proteins with solved structures. To address these limitations, we developed an approach that incorporates cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) data into structure prediction. XL-MS data provide upper-bound distance constraints that can be incorporated into protein deep-learning-based modeling and subsequent docking. Using this approach, we generated a model of two interacting E. hellem spore wall proteins, spore wall protein 1B (Swp1b) and endospore protein 1 (EnP1), which have no clear homologs outside of microsporidia and contain several disordered regions. These proteins are abundant spore wall proteins of microsporidia and previously were not known to interact with one another. The resulting model not only is consistent with the experimental cross-links used to generate the model but was also subsequently confirmed by independently generated XL-MS data. The described AlphaLink-Modeller framework for structure prediction is particularly well suited to proteins with limited homology and/or substantial flexible regions, given that they adopt a defined structural state within a biological context, thereby extending integrative modeling approaches to previously inaccessible targets. IMPORTANCE: In this article, we demonstrate an improved method for the prediction of the structure of protein complexes with no clear homologs and a considerable number of disordered regions. This is significant because these types of proteins are critical to understanding the biology of organisms, yet model generation of these classes has been inaccessible. The method incorporates experimental data obtained from cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) into the modeling process, providing a method to integrate such experimental data into computational modeling of the structure of proteins and protein interactions. For this paper, we have used this method for predicting the structure of two highly abundant Encephalitozoon hellem proteins in the spore wall that are important for host cell infection due to this pathogen of humans and other vertebrates.
abstract_zh: 微孢子虫（如脑炎微孢子虫 *Encephalitozoon hellem*）是专性细胞内人类寄生虫，其基因组难以进行遗传操作，这限制了对它们蛋白质组的功能表征。实验性结构研究具有挑战性，因为微孢子虫中许多蛋白质包含大量无序区域。基于同源建模和深度学习算法的计算结构研究对微孢子虫蛋白质也仍然有限，因为大多数蛋白质与已解析结构的蛋白质几乎没有序列相似性。为解决这些限制，我们开发了一种将交联质谱（XL-MS）数据整合到结构预测中的方法。XL-MS数据提供上界距离约束，这些约束可被整合到基于深度学习的蛋白质建模及后续对接中。利用该方法，我们生成了两个相互作用的 *E. hellem* 孢子壁蛋白——孢子壁蛋白1B（Swp1b）和内孢子蛋白1（EnP1）——的模型，这些蛋白在微孢子虫之外没有明确的同源物，并包含多个无序区域。这些蛋白是微孢子虫丰富的孢子壁蛋白，此前未知它们彼此相互作用。所得模型不仅与用于生成模型的实验交联数据一致，而且随后通过独立生成的XL-MS数据得到确认。所描述的AlphaLink-Modeller结构预测框架特别适用于同源性有限和/或具有大量柔性区域的蛋白质，前提是它们在生物学背景下采用明确的结构状态，从而将整合建模方法扩展到以前无法触及的目标。重要性：在本文中，我们展示了一种改进的方法，用于预测没有明确同源物且具有大量无序区域的蛋白质复合物的结构。这具有重要意义，因为这类蛋白质对理解生物体的生物学至关重要，但此类模型的生成此前无法实现。该方法将交联质谱（XL-MS）获得的实验数据整合到建模过程中，提供了一种将此类实验数据整合到蛋白质结构和蛋白质相互作用计算建模中的方法。在本文中，我们使用该方法预测了 *Encephalitozoon hellem* 孢子壁中两种高丰度蛋白质的结构，这些蛋白质对该人类及其他脊椎动物病原体的宿主细胞感染至关重要。
